data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"No autonomous reclamation protocol is safe under the stated conditions; safety requires an external witness protocol that durably records a signed attestation of evidence absence before reclamation proceeds.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The external witness is compromised or coerced into signing false attestations.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"A lower-level hypervisor or kernel records the workspace terminal state (coredump), providing an ersatz terminal record that makes autonomous reclamation possible after all.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The workspace is provably side-effect-free by construction, rendering the external witness unnecessary overhead.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If the process crashed while holding the workspace and left no terminal record, the system cannot distinguish between (a) a workspace containing completed evidence not yet externalized, and (b) an empty or abandoned workspace. Any autonomous protocol that reclaims the workspace risks silently displacing evidence that was completed but trapped in the crashed process. The only safe protocol is to bind the workspace to an external witness (human operator or audited scavenger) who inspects the workspace and durably records a signed attestation of evidence absence before reclamation is authorized. This converts the epistemic uncertainty into a liability-bearing judgment.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
